A20261008205804.filming: About 35–50 s, vertical 9:16, one continuous take or quick jump cuts. Beats 1–7 are a selfie-style talking head in a casual setting. A numbered list (1., 2., 3. …) is overlaid in a top corner and adds one short line per condition as it is spoken; the last item names Memo AI. Beats 8–10 are a phone screen recording of memoai.eu in the browser, with the creator's voice continuing over it: open Memo AI → upload a PDF/file or use Scan to photograph notebook pages → hard cut past the waiting time → the finished note appears → tap through flashcards, quiz, mind map, podcast and practice test (with its percentage score) → stay on flashcards and flip one card to show the answer. Beat 11 returns to the talking head, or stays on the app screen with a 'comment how far you got' text overlay.
A20261008205804.hook: Talking head, straight to camera, first line is an elimination condition with no intro: 'Ako ti prezime završava na "ić", ispadaš.' The next line raises the stakes: '99% vas neće uspjeti da završi ovu igru.' An on-screen numbered list starts at 1.
not_allowed: Changing the structure: no talking-head elimination game, no growing numbered list, or Memo AI not being the last condition
Introducing Memo AI before the final condition or adding extra product mentions in the game section
Dropping the 'comment how far you got' CTA or replacing it with a sales/discount CTA
Saying you can choose an exam date or target grade, or that the app builds a study plan
Claiming true/false mode, snap-and-solve instant answers to a single photographed task, or checking/grading the user's own homework
Claiming photos can be sent in the chat, PDF export, pasting text, or an Android/iOS app from the store (it is a web app at memoai.eu)
Saying notes are instant: say 'a few minutes' and cut the wait
Showing or naming Astra AI or any competitor
Using conditions that are mean, discriminatory, or about health, religion, ethnicity or politics
Inventing pricing beyond 'one free note, then a 3-day free trial'
A20261008205804.premise: The creator runs a playful 'you're out if…' elimination game. Viewers check each condition against themselves, and a numbered list on screen grows with every line. The last 'you're out' condition is using Memo AI, explained as 'because it's honestly the best study app'. This turns the game into a short screen-recorded demo, and the video ends by asking viewers to comment how far they got.

The wording of each one-line reason, as long as there is one short reason per place
The subject or book shown in the demo, and whether the demo uses Scan or PDF upload
The paper-cutting prop (any repetitive hands-busy hook, e.g. cutting, folding) as long as it is a talking head doing a manual activity
beats: Hook (talking head, cutting paper with scissors): 'These are the top 5 easiest faculties. If you plan to enrol, pick one of these so you won't lose your nerves.'
Place 5: a hospitality/tourism-type faculty, with one reason it is relatively easy (the material is mostly tourism, management and practical things).
Place 4: a management-type faculty, with one reason (not as many demanding maths and natural-science subjects).
Place 3: a business-studies-type faculty, with one reason (the material is understandable, tied to real situations and can be followed with logic, so there is less rote memorising).
Teaser and disclaimer: before revealing places 2 and 1, the creator says every faculty is hard, these are just the 5 easiest, and 'now I'll show you how to make it even easier.'

App demo (exactly 3 sentences, phone filmed over an open book): (1) 'I'll recommend you an app, Memo AI. You just scan the pages from your book with the Scan option or upload the lecture PDF.' (2) 'In a few minutes you get notes, flashcards and a quiz, so you can learn and practise.' (3) 'There's also a practice test that grades you in percent and gives feedback on every answer.'

Place 2: a media/communications-type faculty, with one reason (the material is about communication, media and creative subjects, so there is less cramming), including the natural self-correction 'not learning, I mean cramming'.

Place 1: 'what else could it be', a sport/physical-education-type faculty, with one reason (lots of practical classes, not just book learning, and fewer subjects than other faculties). The video ends on this reveal.
A20261008210957.filming: Length 75–95 s, vertical 9:16, one continuous informal take with natural speech and small self-corrections. Shot A: medium close-up talking head, creator cutting paper with scissors the whole time as the visual hook (beats 1–5 and 7–8). Shot B (beat 6 only): over-the-shoulder/top-down of a phone held over an open textbook. Demo sequence: open memoai.eu in the phone browser → tap Scan and photograph 1–3 textbook pages (or pick a PDF) → jump cut past the few-minute wait → show the finished note → swipe through flashcards → open the quiz → open the practice test and show the percentage score with per-answer feedback. Then cut back to Shot A for places 2 and 1. No on-screen text is required. Optional minimal captions of the place numbers.
A20261008210957.hook: Opening line, said straight to camera while cutting paper with scissors: "Ovo su top 5 najlakših fakulteta. Ako planiraš da upišeš fakultet, upiši jedan od ovih, zato što nećeš gubiti mnogo živaca."
not_allowed: Changing the countdown structure: it must be 5 places, revealed 5→1, with the app demo placed between place 3 and place 2
Dropping the 'every faculty is hard' disclaimer or the 'now I'll show you how to make it easier' bridge
Making it a pure ad, adding a spoken CTA or link push, or mentioning the brand more than once
Naming or ranking specific real institutions (universities/private colleges) as 'easy', or mocking students of any faculty
Claiming Memo AI guarantees passing exams or better grades, or that it makes any faculty 'easy'

Showing or mentioning Astra AI features Memo AI lacks: a 'Priprema za test' subject/material search library, choosing familiarity or mood, snap-and-solve instant answers, homework checking/grading, photos in the chat, PDF export, pasting text
Saying it is an Android/App Store app (it is a web app at memoai.eu), or implying notes are instant (they take a few minutes and the wait is cut)
Claiming it is completely free (only one free note, then a 3-day free trial)
A20261008210957.premise: A student creator counts down the 5 easiest faculties from place 5 to place 1. They add a disclaimer that every faculty is hard and then show on a phone how Memo AI makes studying easier. After the demo they reveal places 2 and 1.
